column1: FIRST, THE THING THAT LOOKED LIKE A FINDING AND IS A COVERAGE GAP
column2: FamilySearch's INDEXED records hold 71 people with the exact surname LUWINSKI in the entire world. NOT ONE OF THEM IS EAST PRUSSIAN.

column1: the breakdown
column2: 22 in "Deutschland, Preußen, WESTPREUSSEN, Katholische und Lutherisch Kirchenbücher" · 13 in "Preußen, POSEN" · 2 in Schlesien · the remaining 34 are American immigration, census and naturalisation, plus the two South African marriages of Kurt.

column1: AND THAT IS NOT A FACT ABOUT THE FAMILY
column2: the Ermland registers are held by FamilySearch AS CATALOGUED FILM, NOT AS AN INDEX. A search of the name index cannot see them. The archive's own Luwinski tree is Posen and West Prussia; Lizzy's birthplace is East Prussia; and the index cannot speak to whether those connect.

column1: and the full-text instrument cannot see them either
column2: FamilySearch full text, which reads unindexed images, returns for LUWINSKI exactly what it returned on 17 September: Milwaukee and Chicago naturalisation petitions, New York passenger lists, Ohio and Minnesota vital records. ALL AMERICAN. The German parish registers are not in that corpus.

column1: *** THE PARISH, AND IT IS NAMED IN THE CATALOGUE'S OWN WORDS ***
column2: catalogue record koha:15497, summary note: "Parish register of baptisms and deaths for GROSS BÖSSAU, Ostpreußen, Germany, now BIESOWO, Olsztyn, Poland. Also includes Kunzkeim, SAUERBAUM, Willims, and Kleisak (Kreis Rössel). Text in Latin and German."

column1: so
column2: SAUERBAUM WAS IN THE CATHOLIC PARISH OF GROSS BÖSSAU, KREIS RÖSSEL. The register series runs 1690 to 1897 and is held on NINE films.

column1: *** AND EIGHT OF THE NINE ARE NOT ONLINE ***
column2: film 7948905 and film 7769256 — the two that matter — both return "Film number not found" in the FamilySearch viewer while signed in. They are catalogued, filmed and shelved, and they are not digitised.

column1: the one that is online was opened and checked
column2: film 102682510, 683 images. At image 591 the camera photographed the film's own title board: "GROSS-BÖSSAU / KRS.RÖSSEL / 1798-1847 / ✝" — the cross marking deaths. So this film really is the right parish AND its baptisms stop in 1792, half a century before anyone in this story.

column1: A MISLABELLING WORTH RECORDING, BECAUSE IT WOULD SEND SOMEBODY AWAY
column2: the FamilySearch image viewer files film 102682510 under "Germany, LUTHERAN Baptisms, Marriages, and Burials, 1500-1971". THE CATALOGUE SAYS "KATHOLISCHE KIRCHE GROSS BÖSSAU" AND THE ERMLAND WAS CATHOLIC. The film's own title board settles it. A researcher who trusted the collection label would conclude these were the wrong registers.

column1: WHAT WOULD ACTUALLY ANSWER IT, IN ORDER OF COST
column2: (1) Films 7948905 and 7769256 at a Family History Centre, where undigitised films can be ordered — Joachim's 1865 baptism would name HIS parents, a generation this archive does not have, and Lizzy's 1893 birth would confirm hers. (2) The originals: the Ermland diocesan archive at Olsztyn (Archiwum Archidiecezji Warmińskiej) and the Polish state archive at Olsztyn hold Kreis Rössel registers. (3) Re-check the two film numbers periodically — FamilySearch digitises continuously, and this is one HTTP request each.

column1: THE CAUTION THAT GOES WITH ALL OF IT
column2: none of this yet puts a LUWINSKI in Sauerbaum. It puts LIZZY there, from a 1939 state document, and it establishes which register would say who her people were. SHE MAY HAVE BEEN BORN AT HER MOTHER'S VILLAGE — Johanna Thimm is of Sauerbaum — IN WHICH CASE THE LUWINSKIS MAY NEVER HAVE LIVED IN KREIS RÖSSEL AT ALL. The register would settle that too, in one line.

column1: # *** ITEMS 16 AND 18 OF THE TWENTY, DONE 20 SEPTEMBER 2026 ***
*** 18. SAUERBAUM IS ZERBUŃ, AND THAT IS THE KEY TO EVERY POLISH ROUTE ***
column2: SAUERBAUM, Kreis Rößel, East Prussia = *** ZERBUŃ ***, today in GMINA JEZIORANY, POWIAT OLSZTYŃSKI, województwo WARMIŃSKO-MAZURSKIE. Its parish and civil district were BÖSSAU — GROSS BÖSSAU = *** BIESOWO ***, today in Gmina Biskupiec, the same powiat. THE AMTSBEZIRK BÖSSAU WAS FORMED ON 9 JULY 1874 WITH ITS SEAT AT GROSS BÖSSAU, so from that date the STANDESAMT BÖSSAU is the registry for Sauerbaum — which is where AUGUSTE "LIZZY" LUWINSKI'S BIRTH OF 28 AUGUST 1893 MUST BE REGISTERED.

column1: why this was worth an hour
column2: every Polish archive, index and portal is organised on the CURRENT name. This archive has spent weeks searching a German one. Zerbuń, Biesowo, Jeziorany, Biskupiec, powiat olsztyński and Archiwum Państwowe w Olsztynie are the words that open the door; Sauerbaum and Bössau are the words that close it.

column1: and it confirms a finding this archive already had
column2: FamilySearch catalogue koha:15497 is "Katholische Kirche Groß Bössau (Kr. Rössel), Kirchenbuch 1690-1897" — read here on 20 September. THE PARISH WAS ALREADY IDENTIFIED CORRECTLY. What was missing was its Polish name and its civil district, and both are now fixed.

column1: *** 16. GENETEKA, WARMIŃSKO-MAZURSKIE — SEARCHED FOR THE FIRST TIME, WITH THE CONTROL PASSING ***
column2: province code 14wm, 278 parishes, KOWALSKI control returns hits. The province-code bug that killed the earlier Szubin attempt was fixed the same day and East Prussia had still never been searched at all.

column1: *** LUWINSKI, EXACT: TWO RECORDS IN THE WHOLE PROVINCE, AND THEY ARE ONE WOMAN ***
column2: 1898 no. 61, Bernhard Pietzkowski, father JOHANN, mother *** ANTONIE LUWINSKI *** · 1901 no. 172, Paul Pietzkowski, same parents. Both at RUSZAJNY (Reuschhagen), Standesamt BARCZEWO-WARTENBURG. No marriages. No deaths. NOTHING ELSE UNDER THE EXACT SPELLING IN THE ENTIRE PROVINCE.

column1: *** AND THEN DAVID SAID TO TRY EVERY SPELLING, AND THAT INSTRUCTION CHANGED THE RESULT ***
column2: this archive had run ONE spelling and written "nothing else under the exact spelling in the entire province" — true as stated and misleading in shape. The archive's own name work records SEVEN forms of this surname. Run one at a time, exact, against the same province, THREE OF THEM RETURN RECORDS AND THE BEST TWO ARE NOT THE ONE THAT WAS TRIED FIRST.

column1: *** LOWINSKI — THREE BIRTHS AT STANDESAMT RÖSSEL, WHICH IS SAUERBAUM'S OWN REGISTRY ***
column2: 1876 no. 68 FRANZ LOWINSKI · 1881 no. 31 ALBERT LOWINSKI · 1884 no. 9 BERNHARD LOWINSKI, all at RESZEL-RÖSSEL USC, parents not carried by the index. *** KREIS RÖSSEL IS WHERE AUGUSTE WAS BORN IN 1893 AND WHERE HER MOTHER WAS BORN IN 1871. *** A Lowinski household is registering children in that district from 1876. It also returns four MORE Pietzkowski children of ANTONIE at Ruszajny — 1895, 1896, 1900, 1903 — so the same woman is spelt LOWINSKI in four years and LUWINSKI in two, by the same registry.

column1: *** LUWENSKI — AND THIS IS THE BEST LEAD OF THE WHOLE SWEEP ***
column2: 1874 no. 11: *** MARTHA LUWENSKI, FATHER JOSEPH, MOTHER ELISABETH BILITEWSKI, OLSZTYN-ALLENSTEIN USC. *** Entry ELEVEN of the new Allenstein civil registry, in its first months. And 1895 no. 692, Alfons Koslowski, mother GERTRUDE LUWENSKI, same registry.

column1: why Joseph matters
column2: JOACHIM LUWINSKI WAS BORN AT ALLENSTEIN ON 21 OCTOBER 1865. A JOSEPH of that surname registering a daughter at Allenstein in 1874 is the right town, the right registry and the right generation TO BE JOACHIM'S FATHER OR HIS ELDER BROTHER. AND THE FAMILY TREE ALREADY HOLDS A "JOSEPH LUWINSKI" WITH NO DATES AND NO PLACE, inside the hundred-name Polish block this archive has always called a surname index rather than a descent. IT IS NOT PROVED AND IT IS THE FIRST TIME THAT BLOCK HAS TOUCHED A RECORD.

column1: the rest of the variants, for completeness
column2: LUWINSKY: zero. LOWINSKY: zero. JUWINSKI: zero. Marriages: LUWENSKI zero, LUWINSKI zero, LOWINSKI one — 1908, Bernhard Lowinski, parents JAKOB LOWINSKI and GERTRUDE BRIESKORN, at Mrągowo-Sensburg USC, which is Masuria and not obviously this family. Deaths: zero under every form.

column1: the lesson, recorded because it was David's and not mine
column2: ONE SPELLING IS NOT A SEARCH. The first pass found one woman in one village. The same index, searched on the archive's own list of documented variants, found a household in SAUERBAUM'S OWN CIVIL DISTRICT and a possible father at Allenstein. EVERY SURNAME SWEEP FROM HERE RUNS THE WHOLE LIST.

column1: what she is worth
column2: BARCZEWO IS WARTENBURG, about twenty kilometres north-east of Olsztyn — JOACHIM LUWINSKI'S OWN DISTRICT, and he was born at Allenstein on 21 October 1865. A woman bearing children in 1898 and 1901 was born somewhere between about 1865 and 1878, WHICH IS HIS GENERATION. She is the first Luwinski this archive has ever found in an East Prussian record. *** SHE IS NOT EVIDENCED AS HIS SISTER OR AS ANYTHING ELSE. *** A rare surname in the right district in the right decade is a reason to look at Wartenburg, not a relationship.

column1: THIMM, EXACT: FIFTY-ONE BIRTHS, AND A CATHOLIC FAMILY WORTH A SECOND LOOK
column2: the Thimms of this province are mostly Protestant and mostly around Mrągowo and Olsztynek. ONE FAMILY IS CATHOLIC AND IN THE RIGHT PART OF THE ERMLAND: FRANZ THIMM and ANNA SCHMIDT of MUNTOWO, parish ŚWIĘTA LIPKA (Heiligelinde) — Barbara 1857, JOHANNA 1859, Francisca 1861, Franz 1863, and then the same couple at Mrągowo-Sensburg in 1873. Święta Lipka is the Ermland's Catholic pilgrimage church.

column1: and the caution on it, which is the whole of it
column2: OUR JOHANNA THIMM WAS BORN AT SAUERBAUM ON 25 MARCH 1871, not at Muntowo in 1859, and Muntowo is in Kreis Rastenburg rather than Kreis Rößel. The 1859 Johanna is twelve years early and forty kilometres away. IT IS A CATHOLIC THIMM FAMILY IN THE RIGHT REGION AND IT IS NOT HERS ON ANY EVIDENCE READ HERE.

column1: *** AND THE COVERAGE BOUND, WHICH IS THE REAL RESULT ***
column2: Geneteka's 278 parishes for this province include OLSZTYN-ALLENSTEIN and its USC, and RESZEL-RÖSSEL and its USC. *** THEY DO NOT INCLUDE BÖSSAU, BIESOWO, JEZIORANY OR ZERBUŃ. *** The two places this family actually came from are not in the index. No Thimm birth of 1871 and no Luwinski birth of 1893 can appear there however the search is run — which is the same shape of answer Szubin gave this morning, and for the same kind of reason.

column1: so the next step is named
column2: ARCHIWUM PAŃSTWOWE W OLSZTYNIE and the STANDESAMT BÖSSAU registers from 1874, plus the Groß Bössau Catholic register before that. That is item 17 of the twenty and it needs a letter, not a search box.
